etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English provynce, from Anglo-Norman province, Old French province, from Latin prōvincia, seemingly corresponding to prō- and vinciō. Replaced Old English boldġetæl.

definitions.definition: A region of the earth or of a continent; a district or country. [from 14th c.]

quote.citation: 1859 November 24, Charles Darwin, “Geographical Distribution—continued”, in On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, […], London: John Murray, […], →OCLC, pages 408–409:
quote.text: […]  we should find, as we do find, some groups of beings greatly, and some only slightly modified,—[…]—in the different great geographical provinces of the world.

definitions.definition: An administrative subdivision of certain countries, including Canada and China. [from 14th c.]

quote.citation: 1798 October 20 [1797], “CALCULATIONS OF THE INHABITANTS OF THE GLOBE.”, in The Rural Magazine‎[1], volume I, number 36, Newark, →OCLC, page 2, column 1:
quote.text: Chowta-Zhin, who is ſaid to be a man of buſineſs and preciſion, and cautious of advancing facts, at the requeſt of Earl Macartney, delivered to him a ſtatement taken from one of the public officers in the capitol, of the inhabitants of the fifteen ancient provinces of China, or China proper, within the great wall ; according to which the number of inhabitants, taken by a regular enumeration, amounts to 333,000,000!

quote.citation: 1911 October 16 [1911 October 15], “CENSOR STOPS REVOLT NEWS.; Troops Moving South, but Number Concealed -- Train Service Reduced.”, in The New York Times‎[2], →ISSN, →OCLC, archived from the original on 2023-08-12, page 6‎[3]:
quote.text: The telegraph administration refuses to transmit messages either to or from the Provinces of Hu-Peh, Hu-Nan, Kiang-Si, Sze-Chuan, Kwei-Chow, and Yu-Nan[sic – meaning Yun-Nan].

quote.citation: 1957, Chung-cheng (Kai-shek) Chiang, “China's Struggle Against Communism: Gains and Losses”, in Soviet Russia in China: A Summing-up at Seventy‎[4], New York: Farrar, Straus and Cudahy, →LCCN, →OCLC, page 236:
quote.text: After the Hsuchow-Pengpu Battle,* with the exception of the battles fought on Tengpu Island and Kinmen Island,** Government troops put up no determined fight, and, as a result, province after province on the mainland fell into Communist hands.

All of Fort McMurray, with the exception of Parson’s Creek, was under a mandatory evacuation order on Tuesday, said Robin Smith, press secretary for the regional municipality of Wood Buffalo in the Canadian province [of Alberta].

definitions.definition: (historical, Ancient Rome, Roman Empire) An area outside Italy which is administered by a Roman governor or prefect. [from 14th c.]

quote.text: He reminded his audience of events in 88BC, when the same Mithridates invaded the Roman province of Asia, on the western coast of Turkey.

Synonym: eparchy (formal equivalent to Latin prōvincia in Greek-speaking Eastern Roman Empire)

definitions.definition: (Christianity) An area under the jurisdiction of an archbishop, typically comprising a number of adjacent dioceses. [from 14th c.]

quote.text: In 1309, neither the Archbishop of Canterbury nor his suffragans would attend in Parliament while the Archbishop of York had the cross borne erect before him in the province of Canterbury.

definitions.definition: (Roman Catholicism) An area under the jurisdiction of a provincial within a monastic order.
(in the plural, chiefly with definite article) The parts of a country outside its national capital. [from 17th c.]

quote.text: To-day the first part of the new Indian Constitution comes into force with the granting of a large measure of autonomy to the provinces.

quote.citation: 2023 February 7, Yauhen Lehalau, “'I Couldn't Just Stand By': Russian Fighters Explain Why They Took Up Arms Against The Kremlin”, in Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty‎[5]:
quote.text: "What are the Russian provinces?" he said. "Dirt, ruins, poverty, drunkenness. That is what we need to be working on, rather than expanding our prison to include Georgia, Ukraine, the Baltic states, and Belarus. That is the kind of Russian nationalist that I am…. There is no sense in using force to hold people that don’t want to be with you."

definitions.definition: (geology) A major region defined by common geologic attributes and history.
An area of activity, responsibility or knowledge; the proper concern of a particular person or concept. [from 17th c.]

quote.citation: 1941 February, “Notes and News: Women on Soviet Railways”, in Railway Magazine, page 82:
quote.text: More than half a million women are now employed on the railways of the Soviet Union, and some of them perform such duties as those of engine drivers and stationmasters, formerly considered the sole province of men.

quote.citation: 1984, Dorothee Sölle, The Strength of the Weak: Toward a Christian Feminist Identity, page 37:
quote.text: Just as money is the province of the economy and truth the province of science and scholarship, so love is the province of the family (Niklas Luhmann).
